Independent standard-deviation and correlation regression

Source: vignettes/joinme-covariance-regression.qmd

Scientific purpose

Marker-by-subject random effects describe departures specific to one subject and one longitudinal marker. Their covariance need not be constant across subjects. A treatment may alter the variability of these departures without altering their dependence, whilst a baseline physiological measurement may alter dependence without changing marginal variability. A single covariance formula cannot express these hypotheses independently.

joinme therefore separates covariance regression into:

  1. a standard-deviation regression, declared by formulaVCov$sd; and
  2. an off-diagonal unit-lower-triangular factor regression, declared by formulaVCov$corr.

Formula interface

The explicit form is:

Code
covariance_formula <- list(
  sd = ~ treatment + age,
  corr = ~ baseline_score
)

A single formula is an exact shorthand for two identical formulae:

Code
formulaVCov = ~ treatment + age

# exactly equivalent to
formulaVCov = list(
  sd = ~ treatment + age,
  corr = ~ treatment + age
)

Both named components must be present when a list is used. Random-effect and the longitudinal time variable are excluded because covariance predictors are evaluated once per subject.

Statistical model

Let Q be the dimension of the marker-by-subject random-effect basis. For subject i, joinme reconstructs

L_i=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma_i)K_i,

where \boldsymbol{\sigma}_i=(\sigma_{i1},\ldots,\sigma_{iQ})^\top contains marginal standard deviations and K_i is a Cholesky correlation factor. The marker-by-subject effect for marker d is

\boldsymbol w_{id}=L_i\boldsymbol z_{w,id}, \qquad \boldsymbol z_{w,id}\sim N_Q(\boldsymbol0,I_Q).

Standard deviations

Let \boldsymbol x_{sd,i} be the design row produced from formulaVCov$sd. For coordinate r=1,\ldots,Q,

\eta^{sd}_{ir} = \alpha^{sd}_r +\boldsymbol x_{sd,i}^{\top}\boldsymbol\beta^{sd}_r +\lambda_{m(r)}z_{L,i,m(r)}.

The marginal standard deviation is

\sigma_{ir}=g_{sd}(\eta^{sd}_{ir}),

where g_{sd} is softplus by default and may be changed to the exponential link with control = list(vcov_diag_link = "exp").

Off-diagonal dependence

Let \boldsymbol x_{corr,i} be the independent design row produced from formulaVCov$corr. For row-major off-diagonal coordinate h=(r,c), c<r,

\eta^{K}_{ih} = \alpha^{K}_h +\boldsymbol x_{corr,i}^{\top}\boldsymbol\beta^{K}_h +\lambda_{m(h)}z_{L,i,m(h)}, \qquad p_{i,rc}=\tanh(\eta^{K}_{ih}),\ c<r.

These partial correlations form one row of the Cholesky correlation factor by

K_{i,rc}=p_{i,rc}\prod_{h<c}\sqrt{1-p_{i,rh}^2},\quad c<r, \qquad K_{i,rr}=\prod_{h<r}\sqrt{1-p_{i,rh}^2}.

The upper triangle is zero and every row has norm one.

The covariance matrix is then

\Sigma_i=L_iL_i^{\top} =\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma_i)K_iK_i^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma_i).

This is the independent regression design: the SD model sets \boldsymbol\sigma_i, and the dependence model sets row-wise partial correlations. The off-diagonal regression is absent when the nested marker-by-subject term uses ||, signalling an iid random effect structure.

Meaning of the latent loading

There is one non-negative scalar \lambda_m for each covariance coordinate. Collectively, \boldsymbol\lambda_L is a vector, not a dense matrix. Its action is

\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\lambda_L)\boldsymbol z_{L,i},

so latent coordinate m affects only predictor coordinate m. In an ordinary model, \lambda_m^2 is the conditional residual variance of that untransformed predictor. It is not itself a final standard deviation, correlation, or covariance.

Priors

Standard-deviation and correlation regressions can have independent priors:

Code
covariance_priors <- jm_priors(
  vcov = list(
    sd = list(
      intercept = prior_normal(mu = 0, scale = 1),
      slope = prior_normal(mu = 0, scale = 0.5)
    ),
    corr = list(slope = prior_horseshoe(
      global_scale = 0.25,
      slab_df = 4,
      slab_scale = 1
    ))
  )
)

Normal, fixed-degrees-of-freedom Student-t, Laplace, and regularised horseshoe families are available. A scalar location or scale applies across its coefficient block; a vector must match that block exactly. The positive lambda_L loadings retain a half-Student-t_6 prior because they describe unexplained heterogeneity rather than observed- covariate regression coefficients.

Fitting

Code
fitted <- joinme(
  formulaLong = y ~ treatment * time +
    (1 + time | id) +
    (1 + time + (1 + time | id) | marker),
  dataLong = data_long,
  formulaEvent = survival::Surv(event_time, event) ~ treatment,
  dataEvent = data_event,
  formulaVCov = covariance_formula,
  priors = covariance_priors,
  families = marker_families,
  assoc = "vcov"
)

summary(fitted) labels SD and correlation slopes separately using their own model-matrix column names. Dynamic prediction evaluates both formulae for the new subject and applies the same unit-lower-triangular factor reconstruction.

The latent-progress entry point uses precisely the same covariance syntax:

Code
mixture_fit <- joinme_mix(
  formulaLong = y ~ treatment * time +
    (1 + time | id) +
    (1 + time + (1 + time | id) | marker),
  dataLong = data_long,
  formulaEvent = survival::Surv(event_time, event) ~ treatment,
  dataEvent = data_event,
  formulaVCov = covariance_formula,
  priors = covariance_priors,
  n_classes = 3,
  formulaClass = ~ treatment,
  class_type = "vcov"
)

The mixture acts on selected standardised covariance coordinates before the SD or correlation link. It does not form a Cartesian product of class allocations for the two regressions. class_type = "corr" selects off-diagonal coordinates; class_type = "vcov" may select diagonal and off-diagonal coordinates.

Exact simulation-to-fit translation

The simulator uses the same formula object and component names:

Code
simulation <- simulate_joinme(
  formulaLong = y ~ treatment * time +
    (1 + time | id) +
    (1 + time + (1 + time | id) | marker),
  formulaEvent = survival::Surv(event_time, event) ~ treatment,
  formulaVCov = covariance_formula,
  truth = jm_truth(
    vcov = list(
      sd = list(
        intercept = c(-0.2, -0.4),
        slope = c(0.35, 0.20, -0.10, 0.05),
        latent = c(0.25, 0.20)
      ),
      corr = list(intercept = 0.15, slope = -0.30, latent = 0.20)
    ),
    re_params = list(
      id = list(sd = c(0.6, 0.2), corr = diag(2)),
      marker = list(sd = c(0.4, 0.15), corr = diag(2))
    )
  ),
  vcov_diag_link = "exp"
)

# Every fitting argument, including data, formulae and fitting priors, is retained.
recovery_fit <- do.call(
  joinme,
  c(simulation$truth$recovery$arguments, list(seed = 401))
)
